text:
mira: Heads-up — after last night's kernel-selector rollout I'm seeing a sizable drop in prefix/prompt cache hit-rate for our conversational workload. Attaching quick numbers below.

ci-bot: perf/job/904: threshold breach (+18% p50 latency). report: https://ci.internal/perf/904 :warning:

sam: can you paste the hit-rate deltas and sample traces?

mira: short summary:
- baseline (before): prefix_hit_rate=82% (16-token prefix), effective_saved_tokens=1.2M/day
- after rollout: prefix_hit_rate=57%, effective_saved_tokens=560k/day
- regression aligns with kernel-selection change at 1769412000

mira: quick trace excerpt:
```
REQ id=abc123 model=gptx-small variant=v1 runtime_meta={kernel=fast_select,hw=amp}
cache_key=prefix::user_utterance::model=gptx-small::variant=v1::runtime_meta={kernel=fast_select}
-> cache MISS, fallback compute
```

jordan: that cache_key looks wrong — we're including runtime_meta in the canonical key. we intentionally shouldn't fold kernel/hw hints into prefix key.

sam: yep. kernel selection is implementation detail, not a semantic part of the prompt. why did selector mutate the key shape?

mira: it was an attempt to avoid serving mismatch when runtime picks a quantized path. selector added the whole request.meta to key instead of a small stable subset. my bad.

kyle: operational impact: unstable keys blow out warmup. repeated retries/stream resumes create many distinct keys so warmup doesn't amortize. streaming resumes are especially nasty (partial KV present but key mismatch => repeated full compute).

anya: SDK-level mitigation idea: add an explicit opt-in cache header so clients can choose canonical key behaviour, e.g., `x-rw-cache-optin: full|stable|off`. default stays on but we can wire it to SDK flag `cache: { behavior: "stable" }`.

sam: propose server-side short-term fix: ignore transient fields in key generation (kernel, hw, trace_id, ephemeral_agent). roll back selector key inclusion. Then deploy a controlled change where kernel variant is mapped to a stable model_variant token (e.g., "gptx-small-int4") if needed for correctness.

mira: agreed. I'll open a small PR to revert key shape and add a sanitization step that strips request.meta except allowed = ["model","model_variant","prompt_normalized_hash"].

kyle: for streaming/retry edgecases we should also accept `x-rw-cache-stable-id` header. SDK can set a single stable id per logical user request across retries/stream-resume. server will prefer stable-id when computing key.

jordan: another perf angle: kernel selector sometimes chooses a slower path that nets better throughput at large batch sizes but penalizes low-latency single-token queries. That interacts with batching heuristics — more misses => smaller batches => higher p50.

anya: can we add a lightweight profiler label to trace to correlate miss->batch-size->latency? even a few counters would help.

mira: yes. plan of action:
1) rollback key inclusion in kernel-selector (hotfix) — mira
2) add request.meta sanitization + unit tests — mira/sam
3) server support for `x-rw-cache-stable-id` and SDK flag `cache.stableRequestId` — kyle/SDK
4) add perf labels and a nightly job to track hit-rate by prompt-length and streaming vs non-streaming — jordan/ci-bot

ci-bot: created perf-issue #498, assigned to mira/sam/kyle/jordan. perf-tracker will start comparing baseline tomorrow. link: https://issues.internal/498 :white_check_mark:

sam: small follow-ups:
- ensure we don't change default semantics for existing SDK users (opt-in only for experimental behaviors)
- document header names in API spec: `x-rw-cache-optin`, `x-rw-cache-stable-id`, and the canonicalization rules

anya: +1 on docs. also add a note about streaming retries: SDK should avoid sending ephemeral nonce per resume; stable-id recommended.

mira: I'll push the hotfix now, will post a short update when rolling out. thanks folks :thumbsup:

kyle: if we need to throttle rollout we can gate by customer tier to reduce blast radius.

mira: noted. cutting hotfix to canary first.

sam: please paste the PR/commit here once created so I can review tests quickly.

mira: PR: https://git.internal/rw/runtime/pulls/1112 — reverting key inclusion + sanitization. running unit tests. will attach perf snapshot after canary.

ci-bot: perf-scan queued for canary @ 1769457000. will report back.

mira: thanks — will follow up with snapshot later today.
